Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The umpires are on the ground and so is the fielding team as they take their positions after last-minute instructions from their captain. Travis Head and David Warner will open the batting innings for Australia as they begin chasing 339.  Aiden Markram is trusted with the new ball to open the bowling attack. Let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, the chase will be up shortly. Australia will chase 339 and South Africa's bowlers will bowl under the lights here. It is still pretty evenly poised as Australia has a good batting lineup. South Africa will hope that the bowlers regain their form in this very important match. Will Australia chase down the mammoth total or will South Africa end up with a victory, their first of the series? Grab a cup of coffee and join us in a while for the exciting chase.

Aiden Markram is up for a chat after a superb innings by him. He says that it was frustrating not scoring runs but you have to analyze with a clear mind and he is happy with his knock but also admits he got a bit of luck as well. Adds that it should be enough for them to defend. Mentions that if the surface plays the same, they are in with a great chance but they are not sure how it would be under lights.

Australia was looking in trouble at the start of the innings as the two openers put up a strong partnership. Mitchell Marsh did a good job of bringing in the spinners, Travis Head and Tanveer Sangha, the debutant into the attack after the drinks break and they rewarded him by dismissing the two set openers. An amazing piece of fielding by Marnus Labuschagne led to the dismissal of Reeza Hendricks. Heinrich Klaasen and David Miller were also dismissed in quick intervals as the bowlers put the pressure back on South Africa. In the last 10 overs, Aiden Markram took apart the bowlers along with Marco Jansen who took apart Nathan Ellis. Ellis however got his revenge in the same over as a blinder from Sean Abbott brought an end to Jansen's innings. The Aussies did not have an answer for the shots Aiden Markram had as he provided his team with a strong end. Travis Head ended up with 2 important wickets along with the debutant Tanveer Sangha scalping one. Josh Hazlewood will be disappointed with his bowling. The target for Australia is 339. It is now up to the batters in the second innings.

South Africa got off to a really strong start as their openers put up a partnership of more than 100 runs. Both Temba Bavuma and Quinton de Kock batted steadily and slowly put the bowlers under pressure. After their quick dismissal, Reeza Hendricks along with Aiden Markram stabilized the innings well. Reeza Hendricks and the new man Heinrich Klaasen were dismissed in quick succession putting the pressure back on the batters. The quick dismissal of David Miller didn’t help the cause and put the hosts on the back foot. In the last phase of the innings, Aiden Markram, who was watching the wickets fall from the other hand, took care of the innings in the end and unleashed an array of shots on the bowlers smashing them all around the ground along with Jansen supporting him playing a cameo. The onslaught from Marco Jansen was stopped by a screamer from Abbott right at the boundary ropes. Aiden Markram continued to find boundaries and pushed South Africa to a very high score of 338 along with staying unbeaten on 102 runs.

Aiden Markram has provided South Africa with a very strong end to their innings. He helped his team put 338 on the board along with bringing up his century. South Africa dominated the start as Quinton de Kock and Temba Bavuma put up a good stand and an explosive finish from Aiden Markram along with Marco Jansen helped them finish just under 340 which is a very good score on this pitch.
